children: First Commonwealth’s net interest income and net income rose year over year in the third quarter, as higher net interest income and noninterest income and lower income tax expense more than offset increased credit-loss provisions and noninterest expense. Net interest margin improved, while lower market rates reduced funding costs.
² Reported as “Net Income”. ³ Reported as “Diluted Earnings per Share”.
: Fully taxable equivalent net interest margin was 4.11%, compared with 3.92% a year earlier.
: Rose 8%, led by higher gains on sales of other loans and assets, swap fees and trust income.
: Provision for credit losses increased to $14.2M from $11.3M, including higher reserves on several commercial loans.
: Commercial real estate loans were 32% of total loans; non-pass commercial real estate loans were $152.6M.
